c74object.name: evi_polyblep
c74object.digest: A GenExpr file, part of 'evieve', for using via 'require()'
c74object.description:
evi_polyblep.genexpr is a .genexpr file and is part of the 'evieve' Package.
It is for using in a gen.codebox~ or in another .genexpr file via the require() command.
By declaring require("evi_polyblep.genexpr"); at the top of a codebox you can then access all of the functions included in this file.
The evi_polyblep.genexpr file also requires:
evi_polyblep_four.genexpr
evi_polyblep_shapes.genexpr
About this File:
Only require this file if you need access to all of the PolyBLEP Oscillators in evieve. It is much more likely that you will require the individual PolyBLEP files ('See Also'). Using the 'poly_osc()' function here you can test all of the two-point Blep Oscillators. The PolyBLEP method antialiases oscillator shapes based on smoothing the discontinuities in a naive signal shape. The best quality in evieve are the four-point Bleps ('evi_polyblep_four.genexpr'). However the two-point Bleps are also very useful ('evi_polyblep_two.genexpr') including interesting morphing Oscillators. The two-point Bleps also offer a wide range of interesting Oscillator shapes ('evi_polyblep_shapes.genexpr').

entry.name: poly_osc ( )
entry.description:
A totally ridiculous 35 waveform switcher intended only for testing / demonstration, not to be used in general
In 1: type=input: freqInHz, Oscillator Frequency in Hz
In 2: type=input: pwm, Pulse Width 0..1 for Oscillators that use it
In 3: type=input: a, Amplitude (linear)
In 4: type=input: t, Phase 0..1
In 5: type=input: dt, Phase Increment
In 6: type=input: morph, Shape Morph 0..1 for Oscillators that use it
In 7: type=input: wav, (int) Oscillator Type 0..36 for selection
Return 1: Osc, Oscillator Output
